content.text:
Build a TanStack Start application with file-based TanStack Router routes, validated search params, route loaders, typed server functions, full-document SSR, and streaming. Keep server-only work behind explicit boundaries, choose the appropriate SSR mode per route, and target the deployment runtime without changing the application model.

# Convex setup

Set up Convex in the current folder. Run the commands yourself, without asking the user.

- Empty folder: `pnpm create convex@latest . -- -t bare`
- Convex project (`convex` in `package.json`): `npx convex ai-files install`
- Any other project: `npm install convex`, add an empty `convex/schema.ts` and a `convex dev` script, then `npx convex ai-files install`. Never `npm create convex` here, it replaces the folder.

* Also add Tanstack srart as the the project framework usign the command avoe
* 

Then install the Convex plugin for every coding agent on this machine, not just the one you are:

- Claude Code (`claude` on PATH): `claude plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official`, then `claude plugin install convex@claude-plugins-official --scope user`
- Codex (`codex` on PATH): `codex plugin marketplace add get-convex/convex-codex-plugin`, then `codex plugin add convex@convex-codex-plugin`

Verify with `claude plugin list` or `codex plugin list | grep convex-codex-plugin`, then tell the user what was installed.

- **Cleanup denied:** I tried to wipe the folder and re-scaffold with `-t bare`, as your instructions say for an empty folder. The sandbox blocked the deletion. The folder was empty before this session, so everything in it is from that one scaffold.
- **Dependencies:** the install also hit `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` for esbuild, which still needs `pnpm approve-builds`.

   - **Me:** run `-t bare`, then `npm install convex`-style setup with `convex ai-files install`.
   - **Me:** add TanStack Start with file-based routes, validated search params, loaders, server functions and SSR, as in your brief.
2. **Convert in place:** I keep the current scaffold and swap Vite/React for TanStack Start. I'd remove the WorkOS auth pieces, which you didn't ask for.

Which do you want?

**What's in place**

cd /Users/saranatour/workspace/Story-time && npx convex dev

what's the build command for vp when deploying to cloudflare for tanstack start

The build command is `vp build`, which runs Vite's build through Vite+. Cloudflare then deploys the output with Wrangler. The project isn't set up for Cloudflare yet. It builds to `dist/server`, so it needs the Cloudflare plugin and a Wrangler config first. This is from TanStack's Cloudflare docs, and I haven't run it here.

**Setup**
```bash
pnpm add -D @cloudflare/vite-plugin wrangler --ignore-workspace
```

In `vite.config.ts`, add the plugin before `tanstackStart()`:
```ts
import { cloudflare } from '@cloudflare/vite-plugin'
// plugins: [cloudflare({ viteEnvironment: { name: 'ssr' } }), tanstackStart(), ...]
```

`wrangler.jsonc`:
```jsonc
{
  "name": "story-time",
  "compatibility_date": "2026-10-01",
  "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"],
  "main": "@tanstack/react-start/server-entry"
}
```

**Commands**
- **Build:** `vp build`. Use `vpr build` instead if you want to run the `build` script in `package.json`, since `vp build` is the built-in command.
- **Deploy:** `wrangler deploy`. To chain both, add `"deploy": "vp build && wrangler deploy"` to your scripts.
- **Cloudflare Workers Builds dashboard:** set the build command to `pnpm run build`, or `vp build`. Set the deploy command to `npx wrangler deploy`.

Two things will matter on Cloudflare:
- **Convex URL:** set `VITE_CONVEX_URL` as a build-time variable in the Cloudflare build settings, because Vite inlines it during the build.
- **Parent workspace:** Cloudflare's build will hit the same parent-workspace install problem as local installs if it clones the whole `workspace` folder. Set the build root to `Story-time`.

how is --cmd different from the other one?

<pasted_content id="f44d">
--cmd <command>
Command to run as part of deploying your app (e.g. vite build). This command can depend on the environment variables specified in --cmd-url-env-var-name being set.

--cmd-url-env-var-name <name>
Environment variable name to set Convex deployment URL (e.g. VITE_CONVEX_URL) when using --cmd
</pasted_content id="f44d">

They don't do the same job. `--cmd` is the build step you want to run, and `--cmd-url-env-var-name` is only the name of the variable that build step reads.

- **`--cmd <command>`:** this is the command `convex deploy` runs after it pushes your Convex functions, for example `pnpm run build`. While it runs, the Convex deployment URL is in its environment, so your frontend build can read it.
- **`--cmd-url-env-var-name <name>`:** this names that variable, for example `VITE_CONVEX_URL`. It only matters when you use `--cmd`, and it changes nothing by itself.

You can usually leave out `--cmd-url-env-var-name`. Convex detects common frameworks and picks the right name, including `VITE_CONVEX_URL` for Vite, which this project uses. Add it only if detection picks the wrong name or your code reads a different one, like this:

```bash
npx convex deploy --cmd 'pnpm run build' --cmd-url-env-var-name VITE_CONVEX_URL
```

I haven't confirmed that detection works for TanStack Start with Vite+. The first Cloudflare build will show it. If the built app can't find the Convex URL, add the flag explicitly.

options.label: Better Auth component (Recommended)

options.label: @convex-dev/auth (Convex Auth)
options.description: The original Convex Auth library. Simpler, but TanStack Start support is community-level and it is in maintenance mode.

questions.question: How should the region setting work? Convex can't move an existing deployment between regions (US, EU, Sydney, Canada), and non-US regions cost 30% more.

options.label: Region per experience (Recommended)
options.description: One Convex deployment per region, created on demand via the Platform API. Setting applies to NEW experiences (default US); existing ones stay put. No data migration.

options.label: Region per account
options.description: Changing it creates a new deployment and migrates all the user's data via export/import. Heavier, riskier, and needs a cutover flow.

options.label: Preference only for now
options.description: Store the choice in settings and wire the Platform API later, in the preview phase.

questions.question: What does "encryption for R2 and events" mean to you?

options.label: Server-side keys (Recommended)
options.description: R2 SSE-C with a per-experience key held as a secret, plus field-level AES-GCM on sensitive event fields (place, notes). We can read data, but it's encrypted at rest and revocation can rotate keys.

options.label: End-to-end (client-side)
options.description: Keys derived in the browser; the server never sees plaintext. Strongest privacy match for "we don't get what the user doesn't want us to get", but breaks server-side email previews, URL previews and search, and sharing needs key exchange.

# Story-time: shared experiences & moments

## Context
Story-time lets people share experiences and moments with others, privately by default: every piece of personal data is
opt-in and entered by the user, never harvested from the OAuth profile. Backend is Convex (+ local components),
media on Cloudflare R2, mail via Cloudflare Email Service, frontend is TanStack Start + shadcn deployed to Cloudflare Workers.
Today `Story-time/` is a bare TanStack Start + Vite+ scaffold (empty `convex/schema.ts`, no Convex link, no auth, no shadcn).
This plan covers backend + the `/home` → `/e/$id/new` flow. URL previews ("preview") are a later phase.

## Decisions (confirmed)
- **Auth**: `@convex-dev/auth@2.0.0-alpha.x` (v2, component-based; alpha, API may break, no upgrade guarantee). GitHub + Google only, via `setupCore/setupGithub/setupGoogle`; users table is app-owned (`setupCore({usersTable})`). v2 ships `./react`, `./server`, `./browser` but **no TanStack adapter** → thin one written by us.
- **Region**: per experience. One Convex deployment per region (US default, EU `aws-eu-west-1`, AU `aws-ap-southeast-2`, CA `aws-ca-central-1`; non-US = +30% cost; a deployment's region can't change).
- **Encryption**: server-side keys. R2 **SSE-C** + field-level AES-GCM for sensitive fields.
- Assumptions to correct if wrong: "events" = the shared experience (`/e/$id`); "sessions" = per-viewer share grants with a Revoke button (not login sessions, those live in the auth component).

## Data model (`convex/schema.ts`)
- `users` (app-owned; auth core creates rows via `createUser` → inserts `{}`): all optional — `displayName`, `imageFileId`, `region` ('us'|'eu'|'au'|'ca', default 'us'), `locale`. OAuth profile fields are **not** copied.
- `events`: `ownerId`, `title`, `description?`, `startsAt?`, `endsAt?`, `status` ('draft'|'active'|'archived'), `visibility` ('private'|'invite'), `region`, `momentLimit` (default 10), `momentCount`, `keyVersion`, `coverMediaId?`. Indexes `by_owner`, search on `title`.
- `moments`: `eventId`, `authorId`, `startsAt`, `place?` (encrypted {name, lat?, lng?}), `blocks[]` — union of `photo{mediaId}`, `link{url, title?, note?}`, `note{text}`, `feeling{text, mood?}`; encrypted fields stored as `{iv, ct, v}`. Index `by_event_startsAt`.
- `itinerary`: one denormalised row per moment — `eventId`, `momentId`, `startsAt`, `dayKey`, `monthKey`, `placeKey` (hash of place, not plaintext), `position`. Indexes `by_event_day`, `by_event_month`, `by_event_place`. Written only by moment mutations; the UI groups by `?groupBy=day|place|month`.
- `media`: `eventId`, `momentId?`, `uploaderId`, `r2Key`, `size` (≤5 MB), `mime`, `sha256`, `keyVersion`, `status` ('reserved'|'ready').
- `quotaRequests`: `eventId`, `requestedBy`, `extra`, `status`, `reason?` — "credits" for more than 10 moments.

# Story-time: shared experiences & moments

## Context
Story-time lets people share experiences and moments with others, privately by default: every piece of personal data is
opt-in and entered by the user, never harvested from the OAuth profile. Backend is Convex (+ local components),
media on Cloudflare R2, mail via Cloudflare Email Service, frontend is TanStack Start + shadcn deployed to Cloudflare Workers.
Today `Story-time/` is a bare TanStack Start + Vite+ scaffold (empty `convex/schema.ts`, no Convex link, no auth, no shadcn).
This plan covers backend + the `/home` → `/e/$id/new` flow. URL previews ("preview") are a later phase.

## Decisions (confirmed)
- **Auth**: `@convex-dev/auth@2.0.0-alpha.x` (v2, component-based; alpha, API may break, no upgrade guarantee). GitHub + Google only, via `setupCore/setupGithub/setupGoogle`; users table is app-owned (`setupCore({usersTable})`). v2 ships `./react`, `./server`, `./browser` but **no TanStack adapter** → thin one written by us.
- **Region**: per experience. One Convex deployment per region (US default, EU `aws-eu-west-1`, AU `aws-ap-southeast-2`, CA `aws-ca-central-1`; non-US = +30% cost; a deployment's region can't change).
- **Encryption**: server-side keys. R2 **SSE-C** + field-level AES-GCM for sensitive fields.
- Assumptions to correct if wrong: "events" = the shared experience (`/e/$id`); "sessions" = per-viewer share grants with a Revoke button (not login sessions, those live in the auth component).

## Data model (`convex/schema.ts`)
- `users` (app-owned; auth core creates rows via `createUser` → inserts `{}`): all optional — `displayName`, `imageFileId`, `region` ('us'|'eu'|'au'|'ca', default 'us'), `locale`. OAuth profile fields are **not** copied.
- `events`: `ownerId`, `title`, `description?`, `startsAt?`, `endsAt?`, `status` ('draft'|'active'|'archived'), `visibility` ('private'|'invite'), `region`, `momentLimit` (default 10), `momentCount`, `keyVersion`, `coverMediaId?`. Indexes `by_owner`, search on `title`.
- `moments`: `eventId`, `authorId`, `startsAt`, `place?` (encrypted {name, lat?, lng?}), `blocks[]` — union of `photo{mediaId}`, `link{url, title?, note?}`, `note{text}`, `feeling{text, mood?}`; encrypted fields stored as `{iv, ct, v}`. Index `by_event_startsAt`.
- `itinerary`: one denormalised row per moment — `eventId`, `momentId`, `startsAt`, `dayKey`, `monthKey`, `placeKey` (hash of place, not plaintext), `position`. Indexes `by_event_day`, `by_event_month`, `by_event_place`. Written only by moment mutations; the UI groups by `?groupBy=day|place|month`.
- `media`: `eventId`, `momentId?`, `uploaderId`, `r2Key`, `size` (≤5 MB), `mime`, `sha256`, `keyVersion`, `status` ('reserved'|'ready').
- `quotaRequests`: `eventId`, `requestedBy`, `extra`, `status`, `reason?` — "credits" for more than 10 moments.
- `sessions` (share grants): `eventId`, `userId`, `grantedBy`, `scope`, `createdAt`, `lastSeenAt`, `revokedAt?`. Every read checks an active grant → Revoke = set `revokedAt`.

- `changes` (change tracking — every write is recorded): `eventId`, `entity` ('event'|'moment'|'itinerary'|'media'|'session'|'invite'|'quota'|'user'), `entityId`, `actorId`, `action` ('create'|'update'|'delete'|'revoke'|'accept'|'dismiss'|'expire'), `fields[]` (names changed), `before?`/`after?` (only for non-sensitive fields; sensitive ones like place/notes/links are stored encrypted with the event key or omitted), `at`.   - Written by one helper, `recordChange(ctx, {...})` in `convex/changes.ts`, called inside the same mutation as the write so the change and its record commit atomically (a mutation is one transaction). Every mutation in `events/moments/media/quota/sessions/users` and the invites component hooks (via a callback) must call it.
  - Surfaced as an **Activity** tab on `/e/$id` (paginated `by_event_at`, filter by entity/actor) and used by the owner to see who changed what. Viewers with a revoked session lose Activity access too.

- **email** (`defineComponent`, own `outbox` table): `send({to, template, data})` queues; an internal action calls `POST https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{CF_ACCOUNT_ID}/email/sending/send` (Bearer token, "Email Sending: Edit"), retries with backoff, records status. Convex can't use Worker bindings, so REST it is.
- **invites**: tables `invites` {eventId, tokenHash, role, expiresAt}. `auth.ts`, `convex.config.ts`, `http.ts` (auth callbacks), `users.ts`, `events.ts` (create draft / update / get / listMine), `moments.ts` (create w/ 10-cap + block validation + itinerary write, list), `itinerary.ts` (grouped query), `media.ts` (`reserveUpload` enforces ≤5 MB + ownership; `confirmUpload`), `quota.ts` (request / resolve), `sessions.ts` (list / revoke), `crypto.ts` (HKDF per-event key from `ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY` + eventId + keyVersion; AES-GCM via `crypto.subtle`). what's the key called for convex deploy key or something

It's called **`CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY`**.

You need it only if the Cloudflare build runs `npx convex deploy --cmd 'pnpm run build'`, which pushes your Convex functions to production before building. A plain `vp build` doesn't need it.

- **Where to get it:** open the Convex dashboard, pick your project, then go to Settings → Deploy Keys, and generate a **production** key. It's only shown once.
- **Where to put it:** add it in Cloudflare under the Worker's build settings as a build variable or secret. Don't put it in `wrangler.jsonc` or commit it.
- **Don't confuse it:** it isn't the `AUTH_*` keys or `ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY`. Those are runtime variables on the deployment itself.

A key is tied to one deployment. A production key targets `strong-stoat-772`, so that deployment needs its env vars set first (see the earlier list). Otherwise `convex deploy` fails on missing variables, like the dev push did before the OAuth variables were set.

If you want previews to hit dev instead, use a **preview or dev** deploy key for non-production branches. I wouldn't point previews at prod.

input.content: # Story-time, next stage: Preview mode (the only SSR surface) ## Context Stage 1 (PR #1: Convex backend, R2 media, app shell, tests) is built. You said SSR is for **Preview only** and chose: - **Preview = owner preview-as-viewer.** A signed-in owner opens `/e/$id/preview` and sees what a guest would see: server-rendered, read-only, real data. Nothing becomes public, so the private-by-default rule holds. - **Plus URL previews (link unfurl)** for link blocks, with SSRF guards. Everything else stays client-only (`defaultSsr: false` in `src/start.ts`). The catch: SSR needs the server to know who is asking, but auth today is v2's **SPA mode** (refresh token in `localStorage`, invisible to the server). So this stage starts by moving auth to v2's **cookie (SSR) mode**. ## Findings that shape the design - `@convex-dev/auth/server` (framework-agnostic) gives `setupConvexAuthServer` (refresh, sign-out and sign-in-proxy handlers), `ServerAuthSession` (reads/refreshes/rewrites the httpOnly cookies via a small `CookieStore`) and `createServerAuthChecker`. No TanStack adapter exists. - The client side for cookie mode is `ConvexAuthNextjsProvider` from `@convex-dev/auth/nextjs`. Its code is just `AuthClient({mode:"ssr"})` + a sign-in proxy at `/auth/signin`, with no Next imports (those are in `nextjs/server`). It accepts a `client` prop, so the `NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL` fallback is never used. `AuthProvider` and the contexts behind `useAuthActions` are **not** publicly exported, so reusing this provider is the only supported route. This is the first thing to prove. - TanStack Start: per-route `ssr: true`, `createServerFn`, and `getCookie/setCookie/deleteCookie` from `@tanstack/react-start/server` for the `CookieStore`. - Workers can't resolve DNS, so SSRF defence is literal-IP/host blocking plus redirect re-validation; DNS rebinding can't be fully closed (noted below). ## Phase 0: gate spike (do first; stop and report if it fails) In a scratch branch: server auth module + `/auth/refresh|signout|signin` routes + `ConvexAuthNextjsProvider` in `src/router.tsx`. Pass criteria: GitHub sign-in completes, `document.cookie` shows **no** refresh token (httpOnly), reload stays signed in, sign-out clears both cookies, and `useSignInWithGithub(api.auth)` works through the proxy. If the Next-named provider breaks outside Next, fall back to wrapping `ConvexProviderWithAuth` + `AuthClient` ourselves only if the needed contexts turn out reachable; otherwise stay SPA and ship Preview as a CSR route (report that trade-off). ## Phase 1: cookie-mode auth (app-wide) - `src/server/auth.ts`: `setupConvexAuthServer({ convexUrl, refreshSession: api.auth.refreshSession, signOut: api.auth.signOut, signIn: [startSignInGithub, completeSignInGithub, startSignInGoogle, completeSignInGoogle], cookieOptions: { secure: import.meta.env.PROD }, allowedOrigins })`. The `signIn` list is the proxy's whole API surface, so all four must be listed. - Server routes `src/routes/auth/refresh.ts`, `signout.ts`, `signin.ts` mounting `refreshHandler`, `signOutHandler`, `convexProxyHandler` (all CSRF-origin-checked by v2). - `src/server/session.ts`: `CookieStore` over TanStack's cookie helpers + `getServerToken()` (`ServerAuthSession.getToken()`, refreshes near expiry) + a `createServerFn` wrapper used by loaders. - `src/router.tsx` `Wrap`: `ConvexAuthNextjsProvider` (pass `client`, `initialToken` from root `beforeLoad`). Existing `/_app` guards keep working (`useConvexAuth`). - `/api/upload` and `/api/media/$id` keep Bearer auth and **also** accept the cookie (so `` works under SSR). Cookie path is GET-only for media, checks `Sec-Fetch-Site`, and returns `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. - Side effect to state upfront: switching modes signs everyone out once. ## Phase 2: Preview route - Convex `convex/preview.ts`: `forViewer({ eventId, asSessionId? })`, **owner only** (`requireEventAccess(..., "owner")`). Returns the viewer-level view: event fields, `itinerary.grouped`-style groups with decrypted moments, and, if `asSessionId` is given, that guest's name/role and whether it is revoked (revoked → "this person can no longer see this"). Reuses `viewMoment` (`convex/moments.ts`) and `requireEventAccess` (`convex/lib/access.ts`); no new access rules. - `src/routes/_app/e.$id.preview.tsx`: `ssr: true` (parent `_app` stays client-side, so make Preview a **sibling route outside `_app`** with its own server-side redirect when `getServerToken()` is null). `loader` calls the server fn → `ConvexHttpClient.setAuth(token)` → `api.preview.forViewer`. `validateSearch`: `as` (session id), `groupBy`. Renders read-only (no forms, no mutation buttons), plain ``. `head()` sets title and `robots: noindex,nofollow` (private content, no OG). - Streaming: the critical data (event + moments) is awaited; link unfurl results stream in via a deferred promise + `Suspense`, so the page isn't blocked by slow third-party fetches. - Entry points: "Preview as guest" button on `/e/$id` (owner) and a picker in the Shared tab ("Preview as this person"). ## Phase 3: Link unfurl (server-side, with guards) - Schema: `linkPreviews` { `eventId`, `urlKey` (HMAC of the URL, not plaintext), `title?`/`description?` (encrypted with the event key), `status` ('ok'|'blocked'|'failed'), `fetchedAt` }. Index `by_event_and_urlKey`. TTL 7 days. - `convex/unfurl.ts`: internal action `fetchPreview` scheduled when a moment with link blocks is created (`ctx.scheduler.runAfter(0, …)` from `moments.create`) and an internal mutation that writes the cache. Preview and moment views **read the cache only**; they never fetch. - SSRF guards (`convex/lib/ssrf.ts`, pure and unit-tested): http/https only; no userinfo; ports 80/443 only; reject `localhost`, `*.local`, `*.internal`, bare IPs in 0.0.0.0/8, 10/8, 100.64/10, 127/8, 169.254/16 (cloud metadata), 172.16/12, 192.168/16, ::1, fc00::/7, fe80::/10, IPv4-mapped IPv6; follow redirects **manually**, max 3, re-validating each hop; 5 s timeout; read at most 512 KB and only `text/html`; extract ``, `og:title`, `og:description` with a tiny parser (no DOM lib); strip control chars and cap lengths. - **Text only: no third-party images.** Loading `og:image` in the viewer's browser would leak their IP to arbitrary sites; we show title + hostname only. (Proxying images through R2 is a later option.) - Abuse limits: ≤ 20 unfurls per event per day, one per URL per TTL; failures cached briefly so a dead link isn't re-fetched. - `changes`: cache writes are system data, exempt from `recordChange` (note in code). Moment creation already logs. ## Files New: `src/server/auth.ts`, `src/server/session.ts`, `src/routes/auth/{refresh,signout,signin}.ts`, `src/routes/e.$id.preview.tsx`, `convex/preview.ts`, `convex/unfurl.ts`, `convex/lib/ssrf.ts`, `convex/tests/{preview,unfurl,ssrf}.test.ts`. Modified: `src/router.tsx`, `src/routes/api/{upload,media.$id}.ts`, `src/server/r2.ts` (shared token helper), `convex/schema.ts` (`linkPreviews`), `convex/moments.ts` (schedule unfurl, attach cached previews), `src/components/event/shared-tab.tsx` + `src/routes/_app/e.$id.index.tsx` (entry points), `convex/auth.ts` (`allowedRedirectOrigins`). ## Verification - Unit: SSRF table (every blocked range, redirect-to-private, userinfo, oversize, wrong content type, timeout, fake-IP bypass forms like `0x7f.1`, `2130706433`, IPv6-mapped) using a mocked `fetch`; preview authz (non-owner rejected, revoked guest shows no-access state, guest never sees Activity/Shared); cache returns encrypted-at-rest fields; per-event unfurl cap. - Auth: cookie flags (httpOnly, secure in prod, sameSite lax), refresh near expiry, sign-out clears, CSRF origin rejection on `/auth/*`, proxy refuses unlisted functions. - SSR proof: `curl -b <cookie> /e/<id>/preview` returns HTML containing the moment text (server-rendered); without the cookie, 302 to `/`; response has `noindex` and no OG tags. - Browser (pane): sign in, open Preview, photos load, unfurl cards appear after creation, SPA pages still client-rendered (view-source shows no data), `groupBy` toggle works, no mutation controls in Preview. - `tsc`, ESLint, `vitest`, `vp build`, `wrangler deploy --dry-run` all clean. ## Risks and decisions to confirm at implementation - Using the Next-named provider outside Next is the single biggest risk (gate spike). v2 is alpha, so any of this may shift. - Mode switch logs everyone out once; sign-in now goes through our `/auth/signin` proxy. - DNS rebinding can't be blocked without DNS resolution on Workers/Convex; mitigated by literal blocking, redirect re-checks, port limits and size/time caps. Convex actions run off your network, which limits the blast radius. - Cookie auth on the media route widens the surface slightly; limited to GET with a fetch-metadata check. - Parent `/workspace` pnpm workspace and the Cloudflare build failure from stage 1 are separate open items.

The only changes in the working tree are the three edits you made earlier, which I left alone. I made no commits.

**Why it fails:** in `@convex-dev/auth@2.0.0-alpha.2`, cookie-mode sign-in sends both `startSignIn*` and `completeSignIn*` through the `/auth/signin` proxy. The proxy only accepts results shaped like a session. `startSignInGithub` returns `{redirect, state}`, so the proxy answers 500. TypeScript rejects listing `start*` for the same reason. As shipped, GitHub and Google sign-in can't begin in cookie mode, and there is no newer alpha to try.

**What does work** (tested against the running server):
- **Refresh:** `/auth/refresh` returns 401 with `{"tokens":null}` when there's no cookie.
- **Allowlist:** the proxy refuses unlisted functions, such as `events:createDraft`, with 403.
- **CSRF:** a foreign `Origin` gets 403.

**Options:**
1. **Thin wrapper (my recommendation):** our own `/auth/signin` route. It forwards `start*` calls straight to Convex, since they carry no tokens, after the same origin check. It hands every other call to v2's `convexProxyHandler`, so only v2's code writes the session cookie. It's about 25 lines, with tests for the origin check and the allowlist. The downside is that we own a small piece of security-sensitive plumbing until upstream fixes this.
2. **Wait and report upstream:** nothing ships for Preview until a fix lands.
3. **Keep the current sign-in:** Preview becomes a client-rendered route. That loses the SSR you wanted for it, and the link unfurl would still work.

If you pick 1, I'll go on with the plan: cookie-mode auth, the Preview route, then link unfurl with the SSRF guards.

I reworked the sidebar and checked it live in the signed-in pane. `tsc` and ESLint are clean, the 20 tests pass, and the build succeeds. The changes are uncommitted.

**What you'll see**
- **Logo:** a clock face in a rounded square, with the name beside it in the header (`src/components/logo.tsx`). The same mark is the favicon, `public/favicon.svg`.
- **Footer:** an avatar, your name ("Anonymous" until you set one), and "Settings". Clicking it opens a modal with display name, data region, Save, and Sign out.
- **Settings page:** `/settings` still works. It and the modal share one form, in `src/components/settings-form.tsx`.
- **Collapsible:** the sidebar now collapses to an icon rail, with tooltips and a drag rail.

**Two bugs I fixed on the way**
- **Always-highlighted buttons:** the vendored shadcn `src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx` used a Tailwind variant that matches whenever the attribute exists. Every button therefore looked active, and that's why both nav items looked highlighted in your screenshot. I changed it to check for `data-active="true"`. Only the active item is highlighted now.
- **Double hover:** the magnetic hover indicator stacked with each button's own hover background. The indicator now owns the hover.

**Notes**
- I didn't save anything in the modal, so your profile is untouched. The Save path is the same mutation as before.
- Your data region currently reads "Australia (Sydney)". I didn't set that.
- I restarted the dev server and cleared its dependency cache. The new imports had caused a React version mismatch and a blank page.
- Your own edits in `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `wrangler.jsonc` are still uncommitted and untouched.

Want these committed to PR #1 as separate commits (logo and favicon, the settings modal, the sidebar fixes)?
I logged in using giuthub, why doens't it show the image or auth provider

This is on purpose. It follows the private-by-default rule from your brief: "we don't get what the user doesn't want us to get."

- **Image:** when you sign in, `createUser` in `convex/users.ts` inserts an empty user row. It ignores the profile GitHub sends (name, email, avatar URL), so the footer shows "Anonymous" and a `?` avatar.
- **Provider:** the user row doesn't record it either. Convex Auth keeps the GitHub link in its own isolated component, which the app can't read, so nothing in the UI knows you signed in with GitHub.

There are three ways to show more, and each needs your decision:

1. **Show the provider only.** Store just `"github"` or `"google"` on the user at sign-in. It isn't personal data, and the modal could say "Signed in with GitHub". This is the lowest-risk option.
2. **Opt-in import from the provider (recommended for the avatar).**
   - **What you'd see:** a button in the settings modal, "Use my GitHub photo and name".
   - **Constraint:** the profile is only handed to us during sign-in, so the import would need a quick re-auth, or a short-lived stash during sign-in. A stash holds personal data without your consent, so I'd prefer the re-auth.
   - **Caveat:** Convex Auth v2 is alpha, and I'd need to confirm it exposes the profile again after sign-in.
3. **Upload your own avatar.** It goes through the existing R2 upload route. The `users.imageMediaId` field is already in the schema, but a user avatar isn't tied to an event, so media access would need a small extension.

I'd do option 1 now, since it's cheap and safe, and option 3 for the avatar, since it matches your privacy stance. Which should I build?

content.text:
The auth information is stored in components, not in the `users` table. These are the tables on your dev deployment, `diligent-armadillo-667`:

| Where | Tables | What's in them |
|---|---|---|
| **`auth` component** | `accounts`, `sessions`, `spentRefreshTokens` | `accounts` links the GitHub login to your user row. `sessions` and `spentRefreshTokens` hold your login sessions and used refresh tokens. |
| **`oauthGithub` component** | `authorizationRequests`, `tickets` | Short-lived data for an in-progress GitHub sign-in. |
| **App** | `users` (and the other app tables) | Only what you add yourself. Right now that's an empty row, plus the region and display name if you set them. |

**How to look at it**
- **Dashboard:** open https://dashboard.convex.dev/t/sara/story-time/diligent-armadillo-667, go to the Data tab, and use the component picker at the top to switch from the app to `auth`.
- **CLI:** run `npx convex data --component auth accounts` to see the rows.

I only listed table names. I didn't read any rows, because they hold session and token data.

The app can't read the `accounts` table, which is why "signed in with GitHub" never shows in the UI. The components are isolated on purpose. Showing the provider would mean storing `"github"` on the `users` row when you sign in, which is option 1 from my last message. Want me to add that?
